newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ASC says JB Were to cut PMP stake to 5 pct.
newsitem.headline: ASC says JB Were to cut PMP stake to 5 pct.

text.p: The Australian Securities Commission said brokerage firm JB Were and Son had agreed to reduce its stake in magazine publisher PMP Communications Ltd to five percent from 10.28 percent currently.

An ASC spokeswoman said the independent broker, one of Australia's largest, had allegedly breached the Corporations Law by not seeking relief from rules which prevent ownership of more than 20 percent of a company without making a takeover bid.
Were had a deemed interest of 40.5 percent in PMP last week in a deal related to its placement of News Corp Ltd's stake after News Corp's sell-out.
Were executive Terry Campbell was not available for comment.
"We have settled this matter so that any conditions which should have applied had JB Were and Son sought relief from us before proceedings, still apply," ASC chairman Alan Cameron said.
"This means that JB Were and Son have agreed to sell down to five percent and will not vote any of the PMP shares until that happens," Cameron said in a statement.
"They have agreed to other requirements, including an external review of their compliance functions, to ensure they operate at maximum efficiency within the firm in future."
